ru: стравливать, стравить (кого-л. с кем-л.); настраивать друг против друга
separable: separable, and nearly always with *against* — *play one buyer off against another*, *play them off against each other*; a pronoun must split it: *play you off*, never ✗ *play off you*
gloss: To set two people or groups against each other so that you gain from the conflict.
examples: She *played* the two dealers *off* against each other and got a better price.
Do not let him *play* you *off* against your sister.
For years the company has *played off* one union against another.

ru: отталкиваться от (игры, реплик партнёра); подыгрывать, взаимодействовать
separable: inseparable here, and often with an extra *of*: *play off each other* or *play off of each other*, never ✗ *play each other off*
gloss: To react to what another performer or speaker is doing and build on it.
examples: The two leads *play off* each other beautifully.
Her solo *played off* the bass line in the first verse.
They have been *playing off* each other's jokes all evening.

ru: подчёркивать, подчеркнуть; выявлять, выявить; обращать внимание на
separable: separable — *point up the difference*, *point the difference up*, *point it up*; slightly formal, and far commoner in writing than in speech
gloss: To draw attention to something and make it stand out more clearly.
examples: The report *points up* the gap between the two schools.
One line in the memo *pointed* it *up* better than any chart could.
The crash has *pointed up* the need for better signals.

ru: срываться, сорваться (на крик); возмущаться; трепать языком
separable: inseparable — the person you are angry at takes *at* (*popped off at the umpire*), the subject takes *about* (*popping off about taxes*)
gloss: To speak loudly and angrily, or to say more than you should.
examples: He *popped off* at the referee and got thrown out of the game.
Do not *pop off* about the layoffs until the memo goes out.
She is always *popping off* about how much better the old system was.

ru: набираться, набраться (смелости); собираться, собраться с духом
separable: fixed in practice — the object is almost always *the courage* or *the nerve*, and it stays after the particle: *pluck up the courage to call*, not ✗ *pluck the courage up*
gloss: To force yourself to find the courage to do something frightening.
examples: It took him a month to *pluck up* the courage to ask her out.
She finally *plucked up* the nerve to tell her boss she was leaving.
I still have not *plucked up* the courage to open the letter.

ru: натягивать, натянуть (одежду); надевать, надеть
separable: separable — *pull on your boots*, *pull your boots on*, *pull them on*; never ✗ *pull on them*
gloss: To put on a piece of clothing with a quick tug.
examples: He *pulled on* a sweater and headed out into the cold.
*Pull* your boots *on* — the yard is still muddy.
She was *pulling on* her gloves as the elevator doors closed.

ru: отчаливать, отчалить; отправляться, отправиться (в путь)
separable: inseparable and intransitive — the place you leave takes *from*: *pushed off from the dock*
gloss: To leave and set out on a journey, especially in a boat.
examples: We *pushed off* from the dock just after sunrise.
We can *push off* as soon as everyone is aboard.
They were *pushing off* before the rest of us had finished breakfast.

ru: загребать, грести лопатой (деньги); сколачивать, сколотить (состояние)
separable: separable — *rake in the cash*, *rake the cash in*, *rake it in*; the bare *raking it in* needs no real object at all
gloss: To earn or collect a large amount of money quickly and easily.
examples: The movie *raked in* forty million on its first weekend.
That food truck must be *raking* it *in* on game days.
They have *raked in* millions from a single app.

ru: ворошить (прошлое); вытаскивать на свет, припоминать (старое)
separable: separable — *rake up the past*, *rake the past up*, *rake it all up again*; never ✗ *rake up it*
gloss: To bring up something unpleasant from the past that people would rather forget.
examples: Why *rake up* a quarrel that everyone has forgotten?
The article *raked up* an old scandal from his college years.
Every election someone comes along *raking* that rumor *up* again.

ru: сооружать, соорудить (на скорую руку); мастерить, смастерить
separable: separable — *rig up a shelter*, *rig a shelter up*, *rig it up*; never ✗ *rig up it*
gloss: To put something together quickly out of whatever materials are at hand.
examples: Dad *rigged up* a shower with a garden hose and a bucket.
We can *rig* something *up* with duct tape until the part arrives.
They had *rigged up* lights over the whole driveway.

ru: сворачивать, свернуть (в трубку); закатывать, закатать (рукава); поднимать (стекло)
separable: separable — *roll up the map*, *roll the map up*, *roll it up*; never ✗ *roll up it*
gloss: To turn something flat into a tube, or to wind something upward.
examples: *Roll up* your sleeves — this is going to get messy.
He *rolled* the poster *up* and slid it into a tube.
She had *rolled up* the car window before the rain started.

ru: подъезжать, подъехать; заявляться, заявиться (с опозданием)
separable: inseparable and intransitive here — *roll up in a taxi*, *roll up at eleven*; never ✗ *roll something up*
gloss: To arrive somewhere in a vehicle, often late or in no hurry.
examples: They *rolled up* two hours late in a borrowed van.
Guests kept *rolling up* long after the food was gone.
He will *roll up* around noon, the way he always does.

ru: растирать, растереть; обтирать, обтереть (насухо); массировать
separable: separable — *rub down the horse*, *rub the horse down*, *rub him down*; never ✗ *rub down him*
gloss: To dry or massage a person or animal by rubbing them hard all over.
examples: The trainer *rubbed* the pitcher's shoulder *down* with ice.
Always *rub down* a horse after a long ride.
She was *rubbing* the dog *down* with an old beach towel.

ru: стираться, стереться; сходить, сойти (о краске, надписи)
separable: intransitive here, so nothing comes between; where the mark lands takes *on*: *rubbed off on my sleeve*
gloss: To come away from a surface because something has rubbed against it.
examples: The price sticker *rubbed off* in my pocket.
Fresh ink will *rub off* if you close the book too soon.
Half the paint had *rubbed off* the railing over the winter.

ru: стирать, стереть (трением); оттирать, оттереть
separable: separable — *rub off the chalk*, *rub the chalk off*, *rub it off*; never ✗ *rub off it*
gloss: To remove a mark or a coating by rubbing it.
examples: *Rub* the chalk *off* the board before the next class.
He *rubbed off* the pencil line and started the drawing again.
The engraving has been *rubbed off* by a century of hands.

ru: стирать, стереть (ластиком); вычёркивать, вычеркнуть
separable: separable — *rub out the answer*, *rub the answer out*, *rub it out*; never ✗ *rub out it*. For pencil marks Americans more often say *erase*
gloss: To remove writing or pencil marks by rubbing them away.
examples: *Rub* that line *out* and try the sum again.
She *rubbed out* the wrong date and wrote the right one above it.
Someone had *rubbed out* half the names on the list.

ru: убивать, убить; приканчивать, прикончить (сленг)
separable: separable — *rub out a witness*, *rub him out*; old crime-movie slang, and always about a person
gloss: To murder someone, in gangster slang.
examples: The boss had him *rubbed out* before he could testify.
They *rubbed out* two rivals in the same week.
Nobody would dare *rub* him *out* in his own club.

ru: откладывать, отложить (деньги); припрятывать, припрятать
separable: separable — *salt away money*, *salt the money away*, *salt it away*; never ✗ *salt away it*
gloss: To save money quietly over a long time, or hide it where no one will look.
examples: He had *salted away* enough to buy the place outright.
She *salts* a little *away* from every paycheck.
They spent years quietly *salting away* cash in offshore accounts.

ru: еле сдавать, сдать; с трудом проходить, пройти; еле-еле справляться
separable: inseparable — *scrape through the exam*, or with no object at all: *he just scraped through*; never ✗ *scrape the exam through*
transitivity: both — transitive (*scraped through the test*), intransitive (*he just scraped through*)
gloss: To succeed at something by the smallest possible margin.
examples: He *scraped through* the final with a sixty-one.
If I study tonight, I might *scrape through*.
The bill has *scraped through* the Senate by two votes.

ru: сожительствовать, жить вместе (без брака); съезжаться, съехаться
separable: inseparable and intransitive — the partner takes *with*: *shacked up with her boyfriend*; informal, and often faintly disapproving
gloss: To move in and live with a romantic partner without being married.
examples: They *shacked up* a month after they met.
Her parents were not thrilled that she wanted to *shack up* with him.
The two of them have been *shacked up* in a cabin all winter.

ru: убираться, убраться; проваливать; отчаливать, отчалить
separable: inseparable and intransitive, and often a blunt order: *shove off!*
gloss: To leave or go away, often said as a rude order to someone you want rid of.
examples: He told the photographers to *shove off*.
The kid *shoved off* the moment he saw the manager coming.
We were *shoving off* just as the rain started.

ru: снимать, снять (пену, жир, сливки с поверхности)
separable: separable — *skim off the fat*, *skim the fat off*, *skim it off*; never ✗ *skim off it*
gloss: To lift fat, foam, or cream from the surface of a liquid.
examples: *Skim* the foam *off* the top before you add the beans.
He *skimmed off* the fat with a wide spoon.
Once the stock has cooled, the grease can be *skimmed off* in one piece.

ru: присваивать, присвоить (часть денег); отщипывать от выручки
separable: separable — *skim off a percentage*, *skim it off*; the source takes *from*, or the fixed phrase *off the top*
gloss: To take part of a sum of money dishonestly for yourself.
examples: A manager had been *skimming off* a few dollars from every shift.
They *skimmed* thousands *off* the building fund before anyone noticed.
He *skims off* a cut of every contract he signs.

ru: резко осаживать, осадить; давать отпор; пресекать, пресечь
separable: separable — *slap down the idea*, *slap the idea down*, *slap him down*; never ✗ *slap down him*
gloss: To reject an idea or rebuke a person sharply, putting them in their place.
examples: The court *slapped down* the governor's order within a week.
Every suggestion he made got *slapped down* in the meeting.
Say it carefully, or she will *slap* you *down* in front of everyone.

ru: сбрасывать, сбросить (кожу); отшелушиваться, отслаиваться
separable: separable when it has an object — *slough off dead skin*, *slough it off*; written *slough* but said SLUF, nothing like *slow* or *slouch*
transitivity: both — transitive (*snakes slough off their skin*), intransitive (*the dead layer sloughs off*)
gloss: To shed a layer of dead skin, or to fall away as such a layer does.
examples: A snake grows a new skin and *sloughs* the old one *off*.
The burned tissue *sloughed off* over the next few days.
This scrub is good for *sloughing off* dead cells.

ru: избавляться, избавиться от; сбрасывать, сбросить (с себя)
separable: separable — *slough off the old habits*, *slough them off*; never ✗ *slough off them*
gloss: To get rid of something you no longer want to carry.
examples: He *sloughed off* his old job title and never mentioned it again.
The company is trying to *slough off* three unprofitable divisions.
She has *sloughed* most of that anger *off* since the move.
